discoveries.finding: The dragon treats giving treasure as part of completing a reciprocal bargain, not as a casual reward.
The fraud becomes more effective when he stops performing obsolete expertise and negotiates from what the dragon is actually doing.
Under the scholar's scrutiny, his useful improvisation separates from his empty bluffing and starts looking like field competence.
The scholar has knowledge he lacks, while he has access and behavioral flexibility she lacks; neither can cleanly replace the other.
Their best joint work requires her doctrine and his live read of the dragon to correct each other in real time.
The dragon may prefer the fraudulent Spotter because he is less attached to ritualized assumptions about what dragons are supposed to want.
Attraction intensifies when the scholar watches him stay present and useful under real danger rather than when they merely trade insults.
Later sexual tension remains strongest when professional trust and competence are under pressure at the same time.
